title: Doubt and Delusion
description: Focuses on the cognitive distortions, emotional attachments, and intellectual clouding that prevent right action and clarity.

subtags.description: The clouding of discrimination where the intellect becomes unable to distinguish between the eternal and the temporary.
examples: Lack of awareness regarding the soul's nature
Intellectual laziness in pursuing Truth
Being covered by the mode of ignorance

subtags.description: The state of being overwhelmed by a crisis of duty, leading to the inability to make a decisive choice.
examples: Arjuna's collapse on the battlefield
Conflict between personal emotion and social duty
Inability to determine the correct path of Dharma

subtags.description: Subtle mental clinging to specific outcomes, people, or objects that creates psychological bondage.
examples: Attachment to family reputation over higher duty
Clinging to the fruits of one's labor
Emotional dependence on external validation

subtags.description: The Divine energy that specifically hides the Truth from those who are not yet prepared to see it.
examples: The inability of the worldly-minded to see God
The covering power of the material modes
The paradox of the Divine being everywhere yet hidden

title: The Subtle and Gross Anatomy
description: Focuses on the biological, energetic, and metaphorical framework of the human machine as a vehicle for the soul.

subtags.description: The five functional divisions of the life-force (Prana, Apana, Vyana, Udana, Samana) that maintain the body.
examples: Balancing the incoming and outgoing breath
The role of breath in steadying the mind
The movement of energy during the yogic exit

subtags.description: The classic metaphor where the body is the chariot, the senses are horses, the mind is reins, and the intellect is the driver.
examples: The intellect directing the mind and senses
The soul as the passenger in the vehicle
The danger of 'wild horses' (uncontrolled senses)

subtags.description: The localized metaphysical and biological center in the heart where the individual soul and Super-soul reside.
examples: The Lord residing in the hearts of all beings
Focusing meditation on the heart center
The source of remembrance and knowledge

subtags.description: The inevitable decay and destruction of the biological shell, contrasted with the eternal nature of the inhabitant.
examples: The body being cast off like old clothes
The inevitable end of all created things
Overcoming the fear of physical destruction

title: The Anatomy of Faith
description: Focuses on the internal conviction, emotional quality, and the sincerity of the seeker's heart.

subtags.description: The stage of spiritual practice where faith becomes immovable and the seeker is firmly fixed in their goal.
examples: Being unshaken by external criticism
Consistent dedication to the spiritual path
Fixed determination in the higher goal

subtags.description: The psychological principle of giving up lower habits by experiencing a superior spiritual satisfaction.
examples: Natural detachment from worldly vices
Finding deeper joy in meditation than in sense objects
Replacing lust with Divine love

subtags.description: The ontological truth that a person's character and future are a direct reflection of the quality of their faith.
examples: A person being made of their faith
The internal belief system shaping external reality
The quality of conviction defining the individual

subtags.description: The intense, sincere hunger to know the Absolute Truth and the purpose of existence.
examples: Approaching a teacher with honest questions
The second category of devotees
Constant search for deeper meaning

title: Chivalric and Political Code
description: Focuses on the ethics of leadership, governance, social responsibility, and the use of power.

subtags.description: The ideal leader who combines administrative power with deep spiritual wisdom and self-control.
examples: Leadership through character and wisdom
The king as a spiritual example for the public
Integrating statecraft with Dharma

subtags.description: The ethical framework for necessary conflict, where force is used as a last resort to protect the righteous.
examples: Fighting against systemic injustice
The warrior's duty to protect the social order
Maintaining moral standards even in battle

subtags.description: The spiritual brilliance and indomitable courage of a leader that inspires others and conquers obstacles.
examples: The undying spirit of a true leader
Mental strength in the face of defeat
Radiating confidence and protective energy

subtags.description: The hallmark of leadership: the ability to put the welfare of the collective above personal gain or comfort.
examples: The leader as the primary servant of the people
Giving up personal luxury for the social good
Directing all efforts toward loka-sangraha

title: The Mechanics of Worship
description: Focuses on the practical methods, rituals, and internal techniques used to connect with and worship the Divine.

subtags.description: The repetitive, focused chanting of sacred sounds to purify the mind and achieve spiritual absorption.
examples: Chanting the sacred syllable OM
Softly reciting the names of the Divine
Using sound vibration to steady the intellect

subtags.description: Routine acts of purification, offerings, and study that ground the individual in a spiritual lifestyle.
examples: Morning prayers and ablutions
Daily reading of the Shastra
Regular acts of charity and sacrifice

subtags.description: The technical and metaphysical focus on the syllable 'OM' as the primordial sound representation of the Absolute.
examples: Understanding OM as the essence of the Vedas
Meditating on the sound vibration of the Absolute
Using OM to begin and end all sacred acts

subtags.description: The culminating act of worship where the seeker offers their entire will and existence to the Divine.
examples: Placing one's life in the hands of God
Total mental alignment with the Divine Will
The final stage of the bhakti process
